findings.title: Prometheus-only Grafana rule actions are not wired to their handlers
findings.body: GrafanaRuleListItem now renders RuleActionsButtons with only promRule, but the menu can enable Grafana-prometheus abilities. The silence menu item is therefore shown and sets showSilenceDrawer, while the drawer is only rendered when a ruler rule exists on line 104, so clicking Silence notifications does nothing. The same prom-only path also cannot expose Pause because AlertRuleMenu requires rulerRule for its pause item, and cannot expose Delete because its delete item is gated by `canDelete && rulerRule`. As a result, Grafana-managed rules in the list lose these actions after ruler loading was removed even when the user has the corresponding permissions.

findings.title: Federated rules are no longer treated as immutable
findings.body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities previously had access to the CombinedRule group and used isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) to disable mutable actions. It now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, where federation is hard-coded to false. Consequently federated data-source rules can receive enabled edit, delete, pause, restore, and permanent-delete UI actions despite the explicit invariant that federated rules must not be edited or removed. This can expose unsupported or cross-tenant rule mutations to users; retain the group federation check or pass the federation state into the lower-level ability hook.

findings.title: Grafana rule view links no longer preserve the originating list URL
findings.body: The replacement list item constructs its view href without the returnTo parameter. The removed GrafanaRuleListItem used createReturnTo() and supplied it to createRelativeUrl, allowing the view/edit flow to return to the same filtered or paginated rule-list URL. Opening a Grafana rule from the new list now loses that context, so returning from the rule view routes users to the default list rather than their prior search/filter state.
